candidates.label: itemLocation

Also called current location, item whereabouts, storage location, physical location. Examples: An archive component has an itemLocation of 'Shelf 3, Box 12'. An archive component has an itemLocation of 'Library Basement'. An archive component has an itemLocation of '123 Main St, Anytown'.

candidates.label: fromLocation
candidates.comment: A from location relation between an exercise, move, or transfer action and the original place of the object or agent before the action occurred. Also called: origin location, starting point, departure place. Examples: "Package Delivery" from location "Warehouse A", "Person Moving" from location "Old Apartment", "Data Transfer" from location "Server Room 1". Distinct from toLocation, which is the destination after the action.

candidates.label: locationCreated
candidates.comment: A creation location relation between a creative work and the place where it was created. Also called: place of creation, origin location, created in. Examples: "Painting locationCreated Paris", "Novel locationCreated London", "Film locationCreated Hollywood". Distinct from location, which refers to the current or general location of an entity.

candidates.label: toLocation
candidates.comment: A destination location relation between an action (like exercise, insert, move, or transfer) and the final place of the object or agent after the action. Also called destination, final location, arrival place. Examples: "MoveAction toLocation 'New York'", "TransferAction toLocation 'Warehouse B'", "ExerciseAction toLocation 'gym'". Distinct from location, which is the general place where something is or occurs.

candidates.label: itemOffered

Also called offered item, demanded item, subject of offer, product/service offered. Examples: An offer has an itemOffered of 'a new car'. A demand has an itemOffered of 'web design service'. An offer has an itemOffered of 'a concert ticket'. Distinct from itemReviewed, which is the subject of a review, not an offer/demand.

candidates.label: location

candidates.label: contentLocation

candidates.label: collectionSize

candidates.label: distance
candidates.comment: A distance relation between an exercise action or travel action and the length travelled. Also called "travelled distance", "route length", "journey distance". Examples: "Exercise action 'Running' distance '10 km'", "Travel action 'Road Trip' distance '500 miles'", "Cycling activity distance '25 mi'".

candidates.label: line
candidates.comment: A line representation relation between a geographic shape and its textual description as a series of points. Also called: path coordinates, point series, geographic line. Examples: "Road Segment line '34.05,-118.25 34.06,-118.26'", "River Path line '40.71,-74.00 40.72,-74.01'", "Borderline line '50.00,0.00 51.00,1.00'".

candidates.label: spatial
candidates.comment: A general spatial relation between a creative work and a place, used when more specific location properties are not applicable. Also called "related to place", "takes place in", "associated location", "geographic context". Examples: "The novel has spatial Paris", "The painting's spatial is a rural landscape", "This document's spatial is the Amazon rainforest.". Distinct from spatialCoverage, which indicates the specific geographic focus of the content.

candidates.label: geographicArea
candidates.comment: A geographic area relation between an audience and the administrative area it is associated with. Also called: target region, audience location, demographic area. Examples: "Local News Audience" geographic area "Springfield County", "National Election Voters" geographic area "United States", "European Market Audience" geographic area "European Union".

relations.embedding_query_text: dedicated to: Describes a museum's thematic focus

instances: Natural History Museum -> Rene Lalique

chosen_property.label: studySubject
chosen_property.justification: Schema.org's studySubject property represents the thematic focus of a museum on a person.

candidates.label: subjectOf
candidates.comment: A thematic relation between a thing and a creative work or event that is about it. Also called "topic of", "depicted in", "featured in", "covered by". Examples: "The person is subjectOf a biography", "The historical event is subjectOf a documentary", "This concept is subjectOf a research paper."

candidates.label: events
candidates.comment: An events association relation between an organization or place and the events connected to it. Also called "associated events", "related events", "features events". Examples: "Organization 'Museum' events 'Art Exhibition, Lecture Series'", "Place 'Park' events 'Summer Festival, Winter Fair'", "Company 'Tech Solutions' events 'Annual Conference, Product Launch'". Distinct from event, which is the singular form.

candidates.label: event
candidates.comment: An event association relation between an action, organization, or place and an event connected to it. Also called "associated event", "related event", "features event". Examples: "Organization 'Museum' event 'Art Exhibition'", "Place 'Park' event 'Summer Festival'", "Inform action event 'Meeting Reminder'". Distinct from events, which is the plural form.

candidates.label: spatialCoverage
candidates.comment: A geographic focus relation between a creative work and the place(s) that are the primary subject or focus of its content. Also called "geographic scope", "covered area", "location focus", "content location". Examples: "A weather dataset has spatialCoverage New York State", "The historical map's spatialCoverage is ancient Rome", "This research paper's spatialCoverage is the Arctic region.". Distinct from spatial, which is a more general spatial association when the specific focus is not known.

candidates.label: displayLocation
candidates.comment: A display location relation between a creative work or product and the place where it can be viewed or experienced in-person. Also called "viewing location", "exhibition place", "experience venue". Examples: "Painting 'Mona Lisa' displayLocation 'Louvre Museum'", "Product 'New Car Model' displayLocation 'Dealership Showroom'", "Sculpture displayLocation 'Art Gallery'".

candidates.label: includesAttraction
candidates.comment: An attraction inclusion relation between a tourist destination and a tourist attraction located within it. Also called contains attraction, destination attraction, features attraction. Examples: "A tourist destination includes an attraction like a museum.", "The city includes an attraction for historical sites.", "This destination features a famous includes attraction."

candidates.label: reviewAspect
candidates.comment: The specific part, feature, or facet of an item that a review or rating pertains to. Also called review focus, aspect reviewed, rating dimension. Examples: `Restaurant Review` reviewAspect `"Service Quality"`, `Product Rating` reviewAspect `"Battery Life"`, `Movie Review` reviewAspect `"Acting Performance"`.

candidates.label: missionCoveragePrioritiesPolicy
candidates.comment: A mission coverage priorities policy relation between a news media organization and a creative work or URL stating its coverage priorities or public agenda. Also called: editorial policy, coverage guidelines, journalistic priorities. Examples: "News Outlet missionCoveragePrioritiesPolicy 'Focus on local news and investigative journalism'", "Broadcaster missionCoveragePrioritiesPolicy 'Public Service Mandate'", "Digital Publisher missionCoveragePrioritiesPolicy 'Transparency and Accuracy Statement'".

candidates.label: studySubject
candidates.comment: An investigative relation between a medical study and the medical entity (condition, therapy, drug, etc.) that is being investigated. Also called "subject of investigation", "research focus", "entity studied", "trial subject". Examples: "The medical study has studySubject a new drug", "The clinical trial's studySubject is a specific medical condition", "This study investigates a studySubject therapy."

candidates.label: aspect
candidates.comment: A specific area or topic of medical practice considered on a medical webpage. Also called: medical topic, health aspect, clinical focus. Examples: "MedicalWebPage 'Diabetes' aspect 'diagnosis'", "MedicalWebPage 'Flu' aspect 'treatment'", "MedicalWebPage 'Cancer' aspect 'prognosis'."

instances: Natural History Museum -> Wingen-sur-Moder

chosen_property.label: containedInPlace
chosen_property.justification: Schema.org's containedInPlace property captures the spatial containment relation between a museum and a city.

candidates.label: location
candidates.comment: A location relation between an action, event, interaction counter, or organization and its physical or virtual place. Also called: situated at, takes place at, found at. Examples: "Conference Event location New York Hilton", "Company Organization location 123 Main St", "Online Meeting location Virtual Conference Room".

candidates.label: containedIn
candidates.comment: A spatial containment relation between a place and the larger place that contains it. Also called "located in", "part of", "within". Examples: "City 'Paris' containedIn 'France'", "Building 'Eiffel Tower' containedIn 'Paris'". Distinct from containedInPlace, which is a synonym, and containsPlace, which is the inverse.

candidates.label: containedInPlace
candidates.comment: A spatial containment relation between a place and the larger place that contains it. Also called "located in", "part of", "within". Examples: "City 'Paris' containedInPlace 'France'", "Building 'Eiffel Tower' containedInPlace 'Paris'". Distinct from containedIn, which is a synonym, and containsPlace, which is the inverse.

candidates.label: locationCreated
candidates.comment: A creation location relation between a creative work and the place where it was created. Also called: place of creation, origin location, created in. Examples: "Painting locationCreated Paris", "Novel locationCreated London", "Film locationCreated Hollywood". Distinct from location, which refers to the current or general location of an entity.

candidates.label: geoWithin
candidates.comment: A geo within relation representing a spatial relationship where a geometry or place is located entirely inside the interior of another containing geometry or place. Also called: is inside, contained in, located within. Examples: "City 'Paris'" geo within "Country 'France'", "Office 'Suite 100'" geo within "Building 'Empire State'", "State 'California'" geo within "Country 'USA'". Distinct from geoContains, which is the inverse relation.

candidates.label: gameLocation
candidates.comment: A game location relation between a game or video game series and a real or fictional place where the game or part of it is set. Also called: game setting, virtual world, game environment. Examples: "Grand Theft Auto V" game location "Los Santos", "The Legend of Zelda: Breath of the Wild" game location "Hyrule", "Assassin's Creed Valhalla" game location "England".

candidates.label: homeLocation
candidates.comment: A home location relation between a person and their residential contact point or place. Also called residence, dwelling, home address. Examples: "A person has a home location in London.", "Her home location is a specific address.", "The individual's home location is a contact point."

candidates.label: foundingLocation
candidates.comment: A founding location relation between an organization and the place where it was established. Also called: place of origin, establishment location, birthplace. Examples: "Microsoft" founding location "Albuquerque, New Mexico", "Apple Inc." founding location "Los Altos, California", "Google" founding location "Menlo Park, California".

candidates.label: applicantLocationRequirements
candidates.comment: An applicant location requirements relation between a job posting and the administrative area(s) from which candidates can apply, especially for remote positions. Also called remote work location, eligible application region, telecommuting area. Examples: "A job posting's applicant location requirements include 'Anywhere in the US'.", "The remote job's applicant location requirements are 'Europe'."

candidates.label: bodyLocation
candidates.comment: A textual description of the location in the body of an anatomical structure or for a medical procedure. Also called: anatomical site, body region, procedure location. Examples: "AnatomicalStructure 'Heart' bodyLocation 'Chest'", "MedicalProcedure 'Appendectomy' bodyLocation 'Abdomen'."

chosen_property.label: amount

candidates.label: amount
candidates.comment: An amount relation between a financial entity (e.g., loan, grant, money transfer) and the monetary value or number associated with it. Also called value, sum, quantity of money. Examples: "A loan's amount is '$10,000'.", "The grant's amount is '€5,000'.", "A money transfer's amount is '250'."

candidates.label: value
candidates.comment: A value relation between a monetary amount, property value, or quantitative value and its specific numerical, textual, boolean, or structured content. Also called amount, quantity, content. Examples: "QuantitativeValue value '10'", "PropertyValue value 'red'", "MonetaryAmount value '99.99'".

candidates.label: price
candidates.comment: A financial attribute indicating the monetary value of an offer, product, or price component. Also called cost, rate, charge, amount. Examples: An offer has a price of '19.99'. A product has a price of '100'. The service has a price of '50.00'. Distinct from priceCurrency, which specifies the currency of the price.

candidates.label: maxValue
candidates.comment: An upper value relation between a monetary amount, property value, property value specification, or quantitative value and the highest value of a characteristic or property. Also called: maximum limit, upper bound, highest possible value. Examples: "Temperature Range maxValue 30", "Age Limit maxValue 65", "Credit Score maxValue 850". Distinct from maxPrice, which specifically refers to the highest price in a range.

candidates.label: minValue
candidates.comment: A lower value relation between a monetary amount, property value, property value specification, or quantitative value and the lowest value of a characteristic or property. Also called: minimum limit, lower bound, lowest possible value. Examples: "Temperature Range minValue 10", "Age Limit minValue 18", "Credit Score minValue 300". Distinct from minPrice, which specifically refers to the lowest price in a range.

candidates.label: priceCurrency
candidates.comment: A financial attribute indicating the currency in which a price or price component is expressed. Also called currency type, monetary unit, unit of exchange. Examples: An offer has a price currency of 'USD'. A product's price currency is 'EUR'. The ticket price currency is 'GBP'. Distinct from price, which is the numerical value.

candidates.label: netWorth
candidates.comment: The total financial value of a person, calculated as assets minus liabilities. Also called personal wealth, financial worth, total assets. Examples: "Person A netWorth '$1,000,000'", "Person B netWorth '$500,000'", "Person C netWorth '$10,000'".

candidates.label: orderValue
candidates.comment: A monetary amount representing the minimum or maximum order value for which specific shipping conditions are valid. Also called order total threshold, shipping value limit, purchase amount condition. Examples: "Free Shipping orderValue '$50.00'", "Discounted Shipping orderValue 'min $100.00'", "Special Rate Shipping orderValue 'max $20.00'". Distinct from orderPercentage, which is a rate based on order value.

candidates.label: returnShippingFeesAmount
candidates.comment: The monetary cost associated with shipping products back for returns. Also called return shipping cost, return postage fee, shipping fee for returns. Examples: `Standard Return Policy` returnShippingFeesAmount `"$7.99"`, `Large Item Return Policy` returnShippingFeesAmount `"$25.00"`, `Free Returns Policy` returnShippingFeesAmount `"$0.00"`. Distinct from `returnFees`, which specifies the *type* of fee, not the amount.

candidates.label: loanPaymentAmount
candidates.comment: A payment amount relation between a repayment specification and the monetary amount of a single payment. Also called: single payment amount, installment amount, payment value. Examples: "Monthly Repayment loanPaymentAmount $1,500", "Quarterly Installment loanPaymentAmount €750", "Final Payment loanPaymentAmount £10,000".

chosen_property.label: amountOfThisGood
chosen_property.justification: Schema.org's amountOfThisGood property captures the quantity of a product stolen in a theft event.

candidates.label: amountOfThisGood
candidates.comment: An amount of this good relation between a type and quantity node and the numerical quantity of a specific good included in an offer. Also called quantity, number of items, item count. Examples: "A shopping cart item's amount of this good is '2'.", "The offer specifies an amount of this good as '5'."

candidates.label: requiredQuantity
candidates.comment: A required quantity relation between a how-to item and the amount of that item needed. Also called quantity needed, amount required. Examples: "A how-to item 'sugar' has a required quantity '1 cup'.", "A crafting project needs a required quantity '5 sheets of paper'.", "A recipe step specifies a required quantity '2 eggs'."

candidates.label: amount
candidates.comment: An amount relation between a financial entity (e.g., loan, grant, money transfer) and the monetary value or number associated with it. Also called value, sum, quantity of money. Examples: "A loan's amount is '$10,000'.", "The grant's amount is '€5,000'.", "A money transfer's amount is '250'."

candidates.label: orderQuantity
candidates.comment: The number or quantity of a specific item ordered within an order item. Also called item quantity, ordered amount, number of units. Examples: "OrderItem A orderQuantity 2", "OrderItem B orderQuantity 5", "OrderItem C orderQuantity 1". Distinct from numItems (for ShippingConditions), which is a limit on total items for shipping.

candidates.label: billingIncrement
candidates.comment: A number specifying the minimal quantity and rounding increment for billing. Also called: billing unit, minimum billing quantity. Examples: "UnitPriceSpecification 'Data Usage' billingIncrement '1' (GB)", "UnitPriceSpecification 'Consulting' billingIncrement '0.25' (hours)."

candidates.label: eligibleQuantity
candidates.comment: An eligible quantity relation between a demand, offer, or price specification and the quantitative value representing the ordering quantities for which it is valid. Also called "valid quantity range", "order quantity limit", "bulk discount quantity". Examples: "Offer 'Bulk Discount' eligibleQuantity 'Minimum 10 units'", "Price specification eligibleQuantity '5-100 items'", "Shipping charge eligibleQuantity 'Over 50 kg'".

candidates.label: offerCount
candidates.comment: The total number of individual offers aggregated for a product. Also called number of offers, offer quantity, total offers. Examples: "Product A AggregateOffer offerCount 10", "Service B AggregateOffer offerCount 5", "Item C AggregateOffer offerCount 20". Distinct from orderQuantity, which is the quantity of a specific item in an order.

candidates.label: loanPaymentAmount
candidates.comment: A payment amount relation between a repayment specification and the monetary amount of a single payment. Also called: single payment amount, installment amount, payment value. Examples: "Monthly Repayment loanPaymentAmount $1,500", "Quarterly Installment loanPaymentAmount €750", "Final Payment loanPaymentAmount £10,000".

candidates.label: numItems
candidates.comment: A limit on the number of items being shipped for which specific shipping conditions apply. Also called item quantity limit, shipping item count, maximum items. Examples: "Free Shipping Conditions numItems 'max 5'", "Bulk Discount Shipping numItems 'min 10'", "Special Rate Shipping numItems '1-3'". Distinct from orderQuantity, which is the quantity of a specific item in an order.

candidates.label: price
candidates.comment: A financial attribute indicating the monetary value of an offer, product, or price component. Also called cost, rate, charge, amount. Examples: An offer has a price of '19.99'. A product has a price of '100'. The service has a price of '50.00'. Distinct from priceCurrency, which specifies the currency of the price.

chosen_property.label: isPartOf
chosen_property.definition: A component or infrastructure project contributing to a broader event
chosen_property.justification: Schema.org's isPartOf property represents the relationship between audit findings/insurance payments and their parent theft event.

candidates.label: partOfSystem
candidates.comment: A biological relation between an anatomical structure and the anatomical or organ system it is a component of. Also called is a component of, belongs to, is found in, forms part of. Examples: The heart is part of the circulatory system. The lungs are part of the respiratory system. A bone is part of the skeletal system.

candidates.label: partOfSeason
candidates.comment: A compositional relation between an episode or clip and the creative work season it belongs to. Also called belongs to, is featured in, is from, is a segment of. Examples: An episode is part of a season. A clip from a show is part of a season. The season finale is part of a season.

candidates.label: hasPart
candidates.comment: A part-whole relation between a creative work and another creative work that is a component of it. Also called includes part, contains component, component of. Examples: "A book has a part that is a chapter.", "A symphony has a part that is a movement.", "A website has a part that is a specific page.". Distinct from includedComposition, which is specific to music compositions.

candidates.label: parentItem
candidates.comment: A hierarchical relation between a discussion item and its preceding item or a creative work it comments on. Also called part of, replies to, refers to, is a response to. Examples: A comment is a parent item of another comment. A question is a parent item of an answer. An answer is a parent item of a follow-up comment. Distinct from comment, which points from something to a comment about it.

candidates.label: partOfSeries
candidates.comment: A compositional relation between an episode, season, or clip and the creative work series it belongs to. Also called belongs to, is featured in, is from, is a segment of. Examples: An episode is part of a series. A season is part of a series. A clip from a show is part of a series. Distinct from partOfTVSeries, which is specifically for TV series.

candidates.label: partOfEpisode
candidates.comment: A compositional relation between a clip and the episode it is a segment of. Also called is a segment of, is featured in, belongs to, is from. Examples: A highlight reel is part of an episode. A deleted scene is part of an episode. A short preview is part of an episode.

candidates.label: partOfInvoice
candidates.comment: A financial relation between an order and the invoice that includes it for payment. Also called is included in, is billed on, is covered by. Examples: An online purchase order is part of an invoice. A service request order is part of an invoice. Multiple orders can be part of a single invoice.

candidates.label: isPartOf
candidates.comment: A part-whole relation indicating that an item or creative work is a component of a larger creative work or resource. Also called component of, member of, contained in, element of. Examples: A chapter isPartOf 'a book'. An episode isPartOf 'a TV series'. A web page isPartOf 'a website'. Distinct from hasPart, which expresses the inverse relationship (the whole *has* a part).

candidates.label: partOfOrder
candidates.comment: A logistical relation between a parcel delivery and the larger order it fulfills. Also called fulfills, belongs to, is a shipment for, is included in. Examples: A package delivery is part of an online shopping order. A food delivery is part of a restaurant order. A furniture shipment is part of a home goods order.

candidates.label: partOfTrip
candidates.comment: A hierarchical relation between a trip and a larger, multi-day trip it is a segment of. Also called is a segment of, is a day of, is a leg of, belongs to. Examples: Day 1 of a vacation is part of the overall trip. A specific excursion is part of a larger travel itinerary. A flight segment is part of a multi-leg journey.
